title: Geopolitical Daily
preheader: Germany blames Russia for airport sabotage; Nepal flood toll tops 1,100.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Wednesday, September 02, 2026 — the 3 stories that matter most today, plus 8 quick updates from around the world.

stories.story_title: US and Iran Trade New Strikes as Six-Month War Escalates
stories.why_important: US forces struck Iran's Larak Island. Iran fired missiles back at US bases in Jordan and other Gulf targets. Trump had said the war was ending, but fighting just grew again. Oil prices and global bond rates are already reacting.
stories.what_overlooked: Most reports on Iranian deaths and strikes come from Iran's state media. No one outside Iran has confirmed these details.
stories.prediction: Watch for Iran to strike Gulf shipping or a base in an allied Gulf state within 72 hours.

stories.story_title: Germany Blames Russia for Airport Sabotage, Expels Diplomats
stories.why_important: Germany says Russia tried to blow up a Ukrainian cargo plane at Leipzig airport using a drone packed with explosives. Berlin kicked out diplomats and tightened visa rules. This is Germany's strongest public claim yet about Russian sabotage on its own soil.
stories.what_overlooked: Germany hasn't shown lab evidence linking the drone to Russian intelligence. The claim relies only on official statements.
stories.prediction: Watch for other EU countries to follow Germany by expelling diplomats or tightening airport security.

stories.story_title: Nepal Flood Death Toll Passes 1,100, Thousands Still Missing
stories.why_important: Nepal's flash flood death toll has risen to 1,127. Nearly 4,000 people are still missing. Rescuers are still searching collapsed hydropower sites a week later. This is now one of the deadliest disasters in Nepal's history.
stories.what_overlooked: News focuses on the death count. It gives less attention to trapped hydropower workers and health risks facing women and girls, as the UN warns.
stories.prediction: Expect the confirmed death toll to keep rising as officials use DNA tests to identify unnamed bodies.

quick_hits.text: China's Xi Jinping arrived in Cairo, his first Egypt visit in a decade, as Iran war reshapes regional alliances.
Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong pleaded guilty to colluding with foreign entities, facing a lengthy prison term.
Taiwan's foreign minister accused China of 'bullying' after Beijing warned of consequences for Taipei's Pacific forum attendance.
The White House named North American Blue Energy Partners to run Venezuelan oil fields once operated by Chinese and Russian firms.
Canada's PM Mark Carney told Washington to 'stop doing memes' and get serious as the US-Canada tariff fight escalates.
European officials protested Russia's finance minister attending the G20 meeting in North Carolina, calling his presence 'discomfort.'
New UK PM Andy Burnham made his first Commons debut, pledging to 'restore hope' amid wars in Europe and the Middle East.
The USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier docked in Thailand after 286 days at sea, a modern record tied to the Iran war.

big_number.context: Nearly 4,000 people remain missing a week after Nepal's catastrophic flash floods killed over 1,100.
